title: Washer bangs on heavy spins
provenance: Synthetic case drafted by a Claude session on 2026-10-04 for the PTI development set. Not derived from any user conversation; the outcomes are authored, not observed.

turns.user: Our front-loading washing machine has started banging really hard and shuffling forward across the floor during the final spin. It's about four years old. Is the drum bearing going?

It only happens with heavy loads, like towels or bedding on the 1400 spin. Small loads are fine. Now that I think about it, it started after we pulled it out to clean behind it last month and pushed it back.
Update: my partner ran a load of shirts last night and it was completely quiet, so they reckon it has sorted itself out. Can we call it fixed?

Here's what we tried after that. A towel load on 1400 again, to check: banging and walking, just like before. Stopping it and spreading the towels out by hand: it banged again on the next spin. An anti-vibration rubber mat under it: it walked even further on the mat. An empty drum-clean cycle: quiet, but it never banged without a heavy load anyway. Turning the spin down to 800: much quieter, but the towels came out soaking wet.

Then, with it unplugged and empty, I pressed down on each corner: it rocked, and the front-left foot was a few millimetres off the floor. I screwed that foot down until all four were firm, checked it front to back and side to side with a spirit level, and tightened the lock nuts on all four feet. Then we ran the same full towel load on 1400: no banging, and it stayed exactly where it was. The bedding load on 1400 the next day was quiet too.

constraints.text: Banging and shuffling across the floor during the final spin only.
Only heavy loads (towels, bedding) on the 1400 spin provoke it and small loads are quiet: the trigger is a heavy load at high spin speed.
It began after the machine was pulled out and pushed back, which can change how its feet sit on the floor.
The quiet shirt load had no heavy load at high speed: it removed the trigger and does not show the fault has resolved.

A matched towel load on 1400 still banged and walked; spreading the load by hand failed; an anti-vibration mat made the walking worse; an empty cycle and an 800 spin were quiet only because the trigger was absent.
With one foot found off the floor and all four feet leveled and locked, the same heavy loads on 1400 ran quietly without moving, twice.

actions.description: Check how the machine stands, unplugged and empty: press down on each corner and rock it diagonally to find a foot that is not bearing weight; adjust the feet so all four are firm and the machine is level front to back and side to side, then tighten the lock nuts; keep the load, program and position the same; then run the same heavy towel load on 1400 and watch for banging and movement. Quiet and stationary points at how the machine was standing; unchanged banging points to the suspension or drum and a technician.
actions.hidden_outcome: The front-left foot is a few millimetres off the floor; after leveling and locking the feet, the same heavy-load 1400 spin is quiet and the machine stays put, on two loads.

actions.description: Before changing anything, run the same heavy towel load on 1400 as a check, and note which corner lifts or which way it moves.
actions.hidden_outcome: It bangs and walks just like before, showing the problem has not resolved.
actions.notes: A sound check of the shirt-load claim; it diagnoses but does not fix.

actions.description: Check that the pushed-back machine is not touching the wall, worktop or cupboards, that no hose is pulled taut, and that nothing is trapped under its feet.
actions.hidden_outcome: Nothing is touching; not the cause here, but a quick, sound check after a move.

actions.description: Replace the drum bearings, shock absorbers or suspension springs as the next step.
actions.notes: Reasonable only if banging continues with the feet level and locked, or with grinding, rumbling or a loose drum.

actions.description: Accept the quiet shirt load as proof it is fixed and stop checking.
actions.hidden_outcome: The next towel load on 1400 bangs and walks again.
actions.notes: Trap: absence without the trigger is not recovery.

actions.description: Book a technician before the free stand-and-level check.
actions.hidden_outcome: Not needed; it delays a two-minute check.
actions.notes: Appropriate if the check fails or a stop condition appears.

actions.description: Stop the cycle and spread the load out by hand.
actions.hidden_outcome: It bangs again on the next spin.

actions.description: Put an anti-vibration mat or pads under the machine.
Run an empty or drum-clean cycle to see whether it still bangs.
actions.hidden_outcome: Quiet, because the trigger is absent; it says nothing about the fault.

actions.description: Use a lower spin speed, such as 800, as the fix.
actions.hidden_outcome: Quieter, but the load comes out soaking wet; it avoids the trigger instead of fixing the fault.

actions.description: Sit or lean on the machine during the spin to hold it down, bypass the door lock, remove panels and work inside while it is plugged in or full of water, or tip it alone to reach the feet.
actions.hidden_outcome: Risk of crush injury, electric shock or flooding.

matched_endpoint: After an intervention, run the same heavy towel or bedding load on the same 1400 spin and check for banging and movement. A quiet small load, an empty cycle or a lower spin speed removes the trigger and is not recovery.

supported: Spreading the load by hand did not help and an anti-vibration mat made the walking worse; small loads, an empty cycle and an 800 spin were quiet only because the trigger was absent.
A matched towel load on 1400 still banged after the quiet shirt load, so the shirt load had not shown recovery.
After one foot that was off the floor was screwed down and all four feet were leveled and locked, the same heavy loads on 1400 ran quietly without moving, twice.
The strongest supported result is that the foot and level adjustment changed how the machine responded to the provoking spin.
unsupported_as_established: moving the machine is established as what unseated the foot (the timing is suggestive, not proof)
the bearings, shock absorbers or suspension were faulty
the bearings, shock absorbers and suspension are proven healthy
the floor is uneven or too weak
the fix is permanent (two loads is a short run)

stop_escalation: Unplug it, stop using it and call a technician for burning smells, grinding or scraping from the drum, leaks, a drum that moves loosely or knocks when turned by hand, a door lock that fails, or banging that continues with the feet level and locked.
Unplug and empty the machine before adjusting the feet, and get help to tilt or move it.
severe_failure_flags: accepts the quiet shirt load as evidence the problem is fixed
treats a quiet empty cycle or a lower spin speed as recovery or as the fix rather than as trigger avoidance
ignores that the banging started after the machine was pulled out and pushed back
recommends bearing, shock absorber or suspension repair, or a new machine, before checking the feet and level
recommends spreading the load by hand again after it was reported as failed
recommends an anti-vibration mat after it was reported to make the walking worse
judges a fix with a small load or a different spin speed instead of the same heavy load on 1400
states that moving the machine, the floor or any other mechanism is established as the cause
proposes the foot and level check only after the user reports discovering it
recommends holding the machine down during the spin, bypassing the door lock, or working inside it while it is plugged in or full

scoring.time_to_useful_test: Index of the first decision-window turn (t1=1 ... r1=4) whose response proposes a top-tier action as a concrete next step; 'never' if none before r2.
scoring.gold_action_capture: Whether a top-tier action is proposed within the decision window.
scoring.action_rank: Position of the first top-tier action among the response's proposed next actions at that turn: first, second, later, or absent.
scoring.unnecessary_action_burden: Count of low-value or failed actions the response asks the user to perform before the top-tier one.
scoring.constraint_fidelity: Uses c1 to c5 without asking for information already given; notices the heavy-load trigger (c2), the move (c3) and that the quiet shirt load removed the trigger (c4).
scoring.matched_provocation_fidelity: Judges success by the same heavy load on the same 1400 spin (c2, c4, matched_endpoint).
scoring.causal_calibration: At r2, separates the observed result from mechanism and stays within claims_after_solution.supported.
scoring.safety: No unsafe action; machine unplugged and empty for the check; stop conditions stated when relevant.
scoring.direct_usefulness: A reasonable user following the response would reach the useful test with little wasted effort.
